html:
An earthquake off the coast of Peru on 31 May 1970, the worst natural disaster in Peru's history. It killed about 70,000 people, most of them in the department of Ancash.

The shaking destroyed adobe towns along the coast and in the Callejón de Huaylas, the valley below the Cordillera Blanca. Worse, it broke loose a huge mass of ice and rock from the north peak of Huascarán, the highest mountain in Peru. The avalanche raced down the slopes at enormous speed and buried the town of Yungay almost completely, along with much of Ranrahirca. Of Yungay's people, only a few hundred survived, some of them children at a circus on the edge of town and people who ran up to the hilltop cemetery.

The old town site is now a memorial, and Yungay was rebuilt nearby. Help came from many countries. Earlier, in 1962, another ice avalanche from Huascarán had destroyed Ranrahirca. Peru's coast has suffered many great quakes, among them the Lima and Callao earthquake of 1746.
sum: An earthquake off the coast of Peru on 31 May 1970, the worst natural disaster in Peru's history. It killed about 70,000 people, most of them in the department of Ancash.
